# Enchantment control integration — provisional playtest

REVIEWED PROVISIONAL MANUSCRIPT. These NEW integration rules accompany seven approved rank-two Enchantment cards. The [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK2_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves the submitted body and records the binding interpretations below. Source originals remain preserved. This is not runtime certification, human balance approval, whole-game closure or GitHub delivery approval.

## Ordinary compelled Attack Actions

When an actual compulsion orders an ordinary Attack Action, use the target's native ordinary attack sequence, including inherent Extra Attack and an NPC's native Multiattack if that is actually its ordinary Action. No additional Action/attack is granted. A source expressly limited to one attack retains that limit: Confusing Flash is such an exception. An ordinary attack instruction is not permission to invent an Attack Action or convert another source's single attack into Multiattack.

Spend required ordinary ammunition normally. The command cannot activate consumable magic, special ammunition with a distinct expendable feature, RP/spellcasting, charges, recharge/per-rest abilities or optional finite-resource riders. Actual optional expenditures remain optional and cannot be compelled indirectly by choosing a method which requires them. Where instruction wording leaves the choice open, the target/controller may use a different legal ordinary method. If none satisfies the instruction, that instruction fails without spending a prohibited resource or manufacturing one. Existing source-specific limits and actual absolute prohibitions remain.

## Application IDs and independently scoped components

Each cast has a distinct application ID. Each component retains its own exact source/caster/target, application identity, deadline and actual defense state. Replacing one component never silently replaces another.

For Dire Charm, successfully established Charmed replaces only that caster's previous Dire Charm Charmed relation. Successfully established servant control replaces only the existing Dire Charm servant component across casters. Charmed-only and servant-only casts can therefore coexist. A successful repeat save, expiry or removal clears only still-active components originating from that application; an old application's save cannot remove a replacement component from another cast. Empty applications have no remaining save schedule. Core Charmed from other sources is unaffected. Shared hard-control history never refunds, even if a component is suppressed or replaced before acting.

## Compelled budget arbitration

This NEW rule resolves collisions among actual active mandatory instructions, including Command, Confusing Flash, Illusive Commands, Dire Charm and Crown of Madness. It does not create commands, extend duration, add repeated control to a one-turn source, grant new target permissions or override an explicit source-specific exception.

Record a priority timestamp for each specific instruction:
- Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands: successful establishment of that failed-save instruction.
- Dire Charm and Crown of Madness: issue of that turn's particular valid order, not the age of the underlying spell alone.
- Simultaneous instructions: underlying effect application order, then a stable source/mechanical ID as the neutral tie-break. Record it before resolving choices; do not decide a favorable order after outcomes.

At execution, gather still-active mandatory instructions and consider earlier priority first. A currently impossible/ineligible instruction claims no budget; proceed to the next. Compatible requirements can share one genuine legal execution. A single Action satisfies two instructions only if that same Action actually fulfills both. Once an earlier valid instruction claims an indivisible ordinary Action/interaction, an incompatible later instruction receives no second copy. Movement uses only the actual remaining movement allowance; sequencing instructions cannot reset spent movement or violate an earlier still-maintained posture/restriction.

A losing ongoing instruction is ineffective only for its contested budget/opportunity, not automatically dispelled. Its compatible independent portions may still operate within existing permissions. Its own endpoint, replacement and saves remain. Priority loss never refunds hard-control history. An invalid later order cannot erase an earlier mandate merely by being issued.

Example: Grovel and an Attack Action may both be satisfied if Prone uses only legal movement/posture and the attack remains legal. Two incompatible ordinary Actions cannot both be demanded from one Action budget. This arbitrates actual compelled behavior; it does not make compulsion optional or restore unavailable actions.

## Six-second control cadence outside initiative

This NEW cadence binds Dire Charm and Crown of Madness's ongoing order/end-save procedures. Other sources retain their actual timing unless expressly bound by a further review.

For a target with no existing initiative/control cycle, successful outside-initiative application begins a six-second virtual target cycle: first START immediately after resolution, first END six elapsed seconds later, then repeated six-second cycles. END resolves before the next cycle's START at the same boundary. Maximum duration remains the original absolute60-second deadline; expiry can end the spell before a later opportunity.

Reviewed procedure: a target shares one active virtual control cycle and one ordinary behavior budget across concurrent control applications. A new application during an already-open virtual cycle does not replay START or replenish budgets; its specifically allowed current-cycle END save still occurs. Each spell retains its own maximum deadline, components and saves. This treats application during an outside-initiative cycle like application during an existing regular turn, preventing repeated casts from creating extra immediate Actions.

The cycle supplies the bound spells' order opportunities, one ordinary six-second behavior budget where needed, and their repeat saves. It does not refresh encounter Reactions, recharge, resources, limited uses or manufacture extra combat turns. If actual combat order becomes necessary, establish ordinary initiative before any not-yet-committed hostile behavior; a virtual cycle is no permission for an extra pre-initiative attack.

Reviewed procedure for entering initiative: map the currently open virtual cycle to the target's first actual regular turn. Carry already received order opportunities and spent ordinary Action/movement/interaction budgets into that turn; do not replay or refill them at its START. The next still-unresolved END save occurs at that actual turn's END. Thereafter use actual regular starts/ends for future triggers. Keep the original absolute duration deadline. Do not replay already resolved virtual events. Existing effects begun in initiative retain their ordinary original virtual-marker rules if they later leave it; this bridge is for these effects first established outside initiative.

Application after an actual regular START grants no order for that already-started turn. A source explicitly permitting an affected current-turn END save still grants that save. Extra turns do not add order opportunities or repeat saves.

## Fixed-zone eligibility history

Calm Emotions and Zone of Truth have fixed spherical centers and require actual exposure/line of effect from that center. Geometric presence behind total cover is not yet eligible exposure. When cover opens around a creature still inside, that moment counts as its first eligible exposure.

Keep one save/acceptance result per creature per spell application:
- Calm Emotions: willing acceptance or the actual WIS save at first eligible exposure.
- Zone of Truth: the actual CHA save at first eligible exposure.
- Success: unaffected by that cast for its remainder, including later entry/cover changes.
- Acceptance/failure: the cast's existing effect is active only while exposed inside its zone; leaving or total cover suppresses it, and restored exposure resumes it without another save.

Acceptance is not a freely toggled dispel choice. Independent zones retain separate casters, concentration, histories and deadlines. Identical restrictions or suppression do not add numerical magnitude. Being unaffected by one zone does not make a creature immune to a different cast.

Calm Emotions suppresses actual Frightened effects, including a newly acquired Frightened source. Create and retain underlying records, ordinary clocks, maintenance and scheduled repeat saves. Once no valid suppressor remains, still-existing effects resume without replaying their original application. A condition which independently expires or is cured while suppressed does not return.

No emotion-themed name automatically disables a class ability. Actual Mooncursed, Momentum Rampage, Divine Fury, Fury of the Host and Beast Empathy source cards have no new emotion-maintenance requirement here. Their real Frightened rider on an affected recipient remains subject to suppression; other printed effects continue.

## Scope and open evidence

The instruction-priority, split-component and zone histories above are authored tabletop procedures, not executed stateful engine implementations. Concurrent outside-initiative applications and the first real turn's carried budget have exact manuscript approval; executable runtime integration remains open. Human testing remains necessary for multiple-attack compulsion, long control without concentration, fear suppression and the unchanged Zone of Truth class-price discrepancy.

## Binding interpretations from the exact review

One-shot Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands do not gain a new repeating cadence from this overlay. If their compelled behavior falls into the same current six-second/regular-turn opportunity, their demands compete for the same actual remaining behavior budget through Compelled Budget Arbitration.

Ordinary actual regular-start processing still happens at the first real regular turn: Reaction refresh, recharge, death-save and start effects follow their normal combat rules. Only the Enchantment control START/order opportunity and already-spent ordinary behavior budget are not replayed. The virtual START was not itself a combat turn or resource-refresh event.

For Illusive Commands, an independently valid soft movement/interaction component that survives a blocked hard Action component establishes a new instruction and replaces the prior pending same-spell record. A saved-against, wholly invalid or wholly blocked instruction establishes no replacement.

A Dire Charm application keeps its repeat saves while at least one of its original components remains. Once it has none, its save schedule stops; an old save never removes a later application's replacement component. No hard-control history is refunded.

Command's Grovel does not inherently consume the ordinary Action. Its required Prone posture can coexist with another legal Action. Confusing Flash's Attack branch continues to spend the ordinary Action on exactly one ordinary attack.

# Rank-three Enchantment integration — provisional playtest

REVIEWED PROVISIONAL MANUSCRIPT. This accompanies eight approved rank-three Enchantment cards. The [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves the submitted mechanics and marked completions. The existing [Enchantment control integration](ENCHANTMENT_CONTROL_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md) remains authoritative in its approved scope. This approval does not certify runtime, human balance, whole-game closure or GitHub delivery. Cosmology remains outside this work.

## Dominate Beast: independent creatures and companion execution

NEW explicit binding: a Beast with an actual independent regular turn receives Dominate Beast orders at future regular STARTs, after ordinary start processing. Outside initiative it uses the reviewed shared six-second virtual control cycle. It shares the same actual budget with coexisting Dire Charm/Crown orders rather than creating another cycle. It has no repeat ending save, so virtual/real ENDs do not create one. Application after the current START grants no retrospective order. Existing ordinary real-start events still occur on entering initiative; already-received control orders/spent behavior budgets do not replay. The original maximum deadline remains.

A dominated Beast using the reviewed owner-attached companion chassis receives no independent turn. At its existing original owner's regular attached companion phase, the dominator may consciously issue a mental order for that opportunity. No extra caster Action/Bonus Action is charged. Actual Dominate Beast control must still exist, the companion must still be eligible and the command must obey its source profile and resource/behavior limits. Without a valid domination order, an already-valid owner command may execute, otherwise only ordinary uncommanded defensive behavior remains.

The forced execution occupies the ORIGINAL OWNER's shared command allowance for that numbered round and, if damaging/offensive under the existing chassis, its shared offensive allowance. These are structural caps; no unwilling owner's Bonus Action, RP or optional feature is charged. The dominator receives no new companion ledger. If another execution already consumed the command allowance, no extra commanded execution is created. If offense is unavailable but the command allowance remains usable, only a legal nonoffensive command can execute. An ordinary owner instruction is not a magical mandatory instruction and has no compulsion-priority timestamp; a valid domination order supersedes a contradictory owner instruction. An owner's already-paid Bonus Action is not refunded.

Reviewed completion — pending commands: redirecting a still-pending command for THIS SAME companion at THIS SAME attached phase reuses that existing execution's structural command reservation; it is not a second command. A still-pending offensive reservation on that same execution can cover the redirected ordinary attack; no duplicate offensive charge. If an existing reservation lacks offense, a new offensive redirection requires the still-free original-owner offensive allowance. Redirecting to a nonoffensive behavior does not refund an already-consumed/reserved offensive allowance. A reservation belonging to another companion, an already-completed execution or another phase cannot be stolen/reused to create this execution. Existing source-specific explicit release rules retain their scope; domination itself grants no refund.

Reviewed completion — phase availability: this bridge uses only a phase that the actual existing companion lifecycle supplies. It does not manufacture an owner phase after that lifecycle no longer permits one, duplicate it on an extra turn, or assign the companion the independent-Beast virtual control cycle. If no ordinary companion execution sequence is active and a commanded combat act matters, establish ordinary initiative with the source owner's existing companion phase. Noncombat work uses only the existing chassis's actual ordinary permissions and finite structural caps; the spell supplies no unbounded off-screen attack/action loop. Missing phase means no commanded execution, while concentration and absolute deadline continue. These bounded completions have exact manuscript approval.

The original companion profile, source-owner stat/DC rules, bond, ownership, slots, HP, Load, upkeep, summon duration, recharge and limited uses remain. Do not restore the original wild animal's discarded attack profile or substitute dominator levels/DC for its attack statistics. The spell's own INT application save uses its actual caster's spell DC. A phase checkpoint supplies no new regular START/END, Reaction refresh, death save, recharge or periodic/duration tick.

NEW exact completion: independent Dominate Beast casts retain separate applications and concentration. At a shared order opportunity their actual mandatory orders use Compelled Budget Arbitration, with timestamp at each order's issue and neutral same-time application/source order. A valid order never duplicates the actual creature/companion budget. Ordinary owner commands remain outside magical priority arbitration. No hard-control history is refunded if another instruction wins or an existing cap prevents execution.

## Hypnotic Pattern: atomic initial application

NEW spell-specific initial resolution:

1. Choose the perceived legal center using actual class-school range: Enchantment 60 feet, Illusion 30 feet; cube extends 15 feet on each axis.
2. Snapshot all creatures inside with actual center line of effect and actual sight of the pattern. Include self/allies when eligible; no selective omission.
3. Resolve each initial WIS save and determine each failed target's independently legal Charmed/Inc components and hard-control allowance.
4. Apply every target's determined initial components and immediate consequences. Actually applied Incapacitated ends that target's applicable existing concentration normally.
5. If the caster's own Incapacitated ends concentration on this Pattern, queue this Pattern's concentration teardown until every snapshotted target has received its initial application. Then remove all still-maintained components from this cast.

No target is skipped merely because it comes later in an implementation loop. Immediate loss of another target's unrelated concentration remains a real consequence even if Pattern then collapses. This is not a universal simultaneous-area or delayed-condition rule. It creates no late application for an initially prevented component.

Helper rousing ends one selected cast's Pattern application on one creature, removing both that cast's remaining Charmed and Incapacitated components. When a helper cannot distinguish multiple actual Pattern sources, use stable application order to select one, without revealing hidden source/caster metadata. Unlike ordinary Sleep's explicit shared wake, one Action does not rouse all Patterns. Positive post-defense/pre-temp-HP damage ends each actually affected Pattern application under its own damage trigger; it does not retroactively change the waking attack's hit/crit.

Recasts form independent sources under actual concentration transitions. An ordinary caster's old concentration ends before a new cast resolves; only a real multiple-concentration feature permits coexistence. Every new Incapacitated attempt checks hard history; independently legal Charmed may remain when hard control is blocked. Charmed-only applications gain no new repeat save. No general illumination, concealment, Speed 0 or ongoing entry aura is created by the persistent visual pattern.

## Terrifying Gaze and Slow: ending-save clocks

NEW explicit binding: Terrifying Gaze and both Slow modes have regular-target-END repeat saves, including an affected current regular turn's upcoming END. This save cadence is distinct from their maximum-duration endpoint. Extra turns grant no extra ending save.

If Terrifying Gaze begins outside initiative, ending saves occur at original application +6, +12 and +18 seconds; its maximum remains +18. An otherwise legally established Slow begun without a target initiative sequence uses ending saves every six seconds after application until its original 60-second maximum. This grants no new outside-sequence Transmutation Reaction trigger.

Reviewed completion — shared END-only cadence: unlike a commanded behavior cycle, these save schedules supply no START/order or action budget. On entering initiative, preserve already-resolved saves and the original absolute maximum. The first still-unresolved save opportunity maps to the target's next actual regular END, then actual regular ENDs supply future saves; never replay a resolved END or add an immediate transition save. If the deadline precedes that next END, expiry ends the effect first. Effects established in initiative retain their original regular/virtual markers on later exit under existing timing rules. This is the explicitly reviewed narrow transition for these new END-only schedules.

Temporary suppression of a condition/rider never pauses the underlying duration or scheduled saves. An actual successful save ends only that source's application on that target, not another independent cast.

## Slow: mode-specific commitments and overlap

Enchantment and Transmutation are separate actual class-school packages. One casting never receives their union. Both retain rank 3/base 5 RP and the preserved per-class level gates.

Transmutation's Reaction window occurs on a perceived creature's own actual turn, including an extra turn, at the beginning of a distinct voluntary movement segment or an Action after commitment and before the first movement step/main outcome. Moving, taking an Action and resuming movement creates distinct segments; choosing another square during continuous movement does not. Each foot/tile is not a trigger. The triggering creature MUST be selected and up to five additional legal perceived creatures may be chosen.

A valid committed Slow is independent of its parent. If a nested legal interruption removes the parent Action, the paid spell still resolves against still-legal chosen targets; it neither refunds nor cancels/revives that parent. The surviving parent continues after LIFO interrupts. Recalculate remaining movement before its next expenditure using actual current Speed and the unchanged spent-movement ledger. A no-Reactions rider bars future commitments only; a Reaction already legally committed in the stack is not canceled by that rider.

Enchantment's one-Action ceiling counts full Actions already committed on that actual turn. It blocks a future commitment once one is already committed, while an already-committed second Action finishes. Each actual extra turn has its own ceiling; the source grants no extra turn. Actual extra-Action resources may exist but cannot be newly committed contrary to the active ceiling. Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement and inherent attacks inside one legal Attack Action remain.

The Enchantment DEX rider is exactly -2 Dexterity ability checks/saves EXCEPT initiative; it changes no score/modifier, attack, damage, spell DC or unnamed derived value. AC gets its separate -2 only. Half-Speed uses existing strongest-adverse-Speed arbitration against the shared pre-control Speed, followed by the existing later systemic multipliers. Actual narrowly scoped defenses can suppress/block one component without erasing the others. Neither an Action ceiling retaining the ordinary Action nor Reaction denial claims whole-Action hard control.

Each source keeps its own concentration/save/deadline. Same Slow half-Speed/-2 AC/-2 DEX riders do not add magnitude. Distinct active Enchantment/Transmutation riders can coexist through separate casts; ending one exposes whichever other sources remain, not a merged permanent package.

## Suggestion: task scope and hard-control reservation

NEW binding: Suggestion's persistent mandatory instruction uses its successful establishment timestamp for Compelled Budget Arbitration. It retains that priority while genuinely active, but never supplies an extra budget or overrides an earlier applicable absolute restriction. Actual task permissions and reasonable legal details remain as authored on the card.

If the stated task necessarily requires whole ordinary Actions, including after an awaited conditional trigger, establish and claim the hard component once when Suggestion establishes. Do not reserve afresh per later Action. When blocked, only an independently meaningful legal soft task can establish. That surviving task may replace a prior Suggestion; an attempt with no legal meaningful task does not.

A task established without hard control cannot acquire it dynamically. If changed circumstances require an unreserved whole Action, seek an achievable reasonable path within the original soft permissions, such as waiting for an ordinary door opening. If none remains, end the remaining compulsion. Ordinary temporary delay/inconvenience is not itself cancellation. Neither caster nor target/controller may reword the task to create a new hard permission or extend its original eight-hour deadline.

An actually reasonable hostile task can direct the target's actual ordinary Attack Action/native attack sequence and required mundane ammunition; it does not compel optional finite features, special expendable ammunition, spells/RP or other forbidden expenditures. Reasonableness uses actual target beliefs/loyalties/knowledge/circumstances after payment without a caster diagnostic. Bonus Actions, Reactions and separately granted extra Actions are not commandeered. No repeating control cycle is added outside initiative.

## Scope and open validation

The companion pending-command/phase completions, independent Dominate Beast same-spell records, END-only transition, and Mental Chains voluntary-transport/plane completions on its card have exact manuscript approval. The Hypnotic Pattern batch is spell-specific. All prior 229 operational card records and actual source/class files remain unchanged. These are authored procedures, not executed scheduler or companion-control implementations. Human tests remain required for four-target Stunned, sustained native attacks, area Incapacitated, eight-hour Suggestion, no-repeat-save Fear and six-target Reaction Slow.

## Mental Chains: binding separated-plane interpretation

If a creature is involuntarily moved away from an application's anchor plane, that application's voluntary-distance/plane restriction has no effect while the creature remains separated. Ordinary rules govern further travel from that other plane, including voluntary travel elsewhere or return to the anchor plane. Concentration and the original deadline continue. On return, that application's original fixed anchor and boundary resume immediately. Another independent Mental Chains application on the creature's current plane still retains its own actual restrictions. This is the exact review's interpretation of the approved separation/resumption procedure, not a cosmology ruling.

# Shared rules for the class playtest drafts

**Provisional design integration, 8 October 2026.** These rules make the class drafts usable together for testing. They preserve each protected class engine while specifying missing timing and replacing conflicting old percentages. They do not rewrite the approved Word books. Original descriptions and alternate registry entries remain in `data/playtest/class_sources`.

## Reading a class card

Use the class's own level, never total character level, for gates and effects. **L** means that class level; **S** is 1/2/3/4 at class levels 1/5/11/17. **M** means max(1, the class ability modifier), for effect a mounts only. Attacks use d20 + normal character proficiency + the actual appropriate ability modifier. Class save DC is 8 + normal proficiency + actual class ability modifier. Negative modifiers still apply to attacks and DCs. One tile is 5 ft. Fractions round down unless specified. Distances cannot be negative.

A weapon attack uses its usual ability, weapon die and damage type. A technique that says “make one weapon attack” replaces your Action with that attack; it does not also grant a normal Attack Action or Extra Attack. Generic attack-speed language has no effect beyond the exact attacks printed in the draft. A spell attack uses the class's stated casting ability. Natural 1 misses and natural 20 hits/critically doubles damage dice; flat bonuses do not double. A save succeeds at DC; “fails by 10” means the total is at least 10 below DC. Critical-range improvements never stack; use the broadest one.

An ability is known only if granted or selected by the draft schedule. Satisfy all printed prerequisites, target legality, action availability, recharge and resource costs before spending anything. A failed legal attack/save attempt still pays; an illegal activation spends nothing. No resource goes below 0 or above its cap. A class feature name shared with a spell does not grant both versions; use the version selected, with its own cost and timing. Names and source text are preserved; the current card is the operational draft.

## Action and timing limits

One regular Action, one Bonus Action if a feature permits it, normal movement and one Reaction between starts of your turns. A free trigger costs no Action only if expressly stated. All grants share **one extra full Action per creature per round**. An extra Action cannot grant another Action, recharge itself, or start another extra-Action grant. It supplies no extra Bonus Action or Reaction. A card granting additional attacks is not permission to repeat all class riders on every hit: obey each rider's frequency.

Recharge N sets a counter to N after use; reduce once at the start of the owner's regular initiative turn, whether able to act or not. Extra turns/Actions do not tick it. Outside combat tick once per 6 elapsed seconds, without double counting. Recharge 2 used on turn 1 is ready on turn 3. A positive counter can be reset/shortened at most once per ability per round. Zero counters are not legal reset targets and expend no reset use. Resets never restore RP or per-rest uses or grant an immediate activation.

An encounter is a genuine scene of uncertain opposition chosen by the Director, not a player declaration used to reset resources. No encounter gain from attacking allies, one's summons, harmless animals, helpless captives or reused corpses. Out-of-combat abilities retain all printed costs and time. Short-rest means a completed uninterrupted hour of permitted recovery; long-rest means a completed 8-hour Rest Watch. This time convention is a draft integration. Expedition pressure, supplies, safe locations and rest debt still matter. A long rest also refreshes short-rest uses; a short rest never refreshes long-rest uses. Weekly uses refresh after seven full in-world days, not repeated rests.

## Targets, concentration and control

Unless expressly stated, perceive the target, remain within range and have line of effect; total cover blocks targeting. “Ally” includes self unless it says OTHER. A list cannot contain a creature twice. Select up to the printed limit; an empty target list is not a valid way to farm activation benefits. Zones remain at their chosen point unless described as an aura; allies can leave and lose their benefits. An aura requires its owner conscious unless the card supplies a bounded exception. An effect ending at “end next turn” means the affected creature's next turn only when the card says target's; otherwise the user's.

One concentration slot for all spells, Chants, Veinweaves, forms or zones that require concentration. Starting another ends the old before the new effect resolves, except for an explicit limited linked-effect rule. Damage prompts CON save against max(10, floor(damage/2)); incapacitation or a failed save ends concentration. The round-down convention is a deliberate pilot interpretation. Concentration does not demand a Bonus Action unless maintenance says so. For a paid 3-pulse effect, start is pulse 1; pay maintenance on each of the next 2 regular turns by turn end for pulses 2/3. Missing payment ends it at that turn's end; otherwise it ends at start of turn 4. No repeated start triggers on maintenance.

Forced movement does not provoke opportunity attacks unless explicitly stated, cannot place a creature inside solid matter, and stops at an obstacle. Grapples use the card's save/DC, can be escaped with an Action and STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against that DC, and end beyond reach. A root sets Speed 0 but does not remove Actions. Slows reduce Speed to minimum 0. Silence blocks verbal spells/audible abilities, not all thought or all class features. Charmed effects never determine a player's beliefs; use only the printed action restrictions.

No repeated hard denial without a new save and cost. For this class suite, a creature can suffer **Stunned, compelled loss of its whole Action/turn, or equivalent hard denial from a given character at most once per encounter**, across that character's class features; later such riders fail while damage and soft riders resolve normally. Record source and target. This draft guard is broader than the older Oracle-only ceiling and is an explicit balance proposal. Reaction denial, Speed reduction, penalties and Frightened do not count as whole-turn loss. Do not silently waive boss immunities, legendary defenses or anatomy.

## Damage, healing, stacking and companions

Roll once for each shared area/pulse and apply saves/defenses to each target separately; separate attacks roll separately. Halve once for a successful save and apply resistance/immunity normally. Same-named conditions/bonuses do not stack unless a printed cap allows it; same-stat flat bonuses from these class techniques use the strongest. Different resources remain separate. Damage reduction from these class features uses the strongest flat reduction, then applies resistance; it cannot create negative damage or healing. Temporary HP never stack; choose the larger remaining amount. Immunity is not reduced resistance.

Repeated permanent HP recovery must consume finite RP, a per-rest use or another finite resource; a combat-generated gauge alone never enables unlimited healing. Healing cannot exceed maximum HP or erase Wounds, death consequences, debt or Corruption unless explicit. Downed is living at 0 HP; dead is different. Resurrection requires a willing soul and sufficiently intact body, obeys its time window, cannot create a duplicate and never refunds the feature on failure to meet known prerequisites. Sacrificial HP is actual unpreventable loss, cannot be redirected or paid with temporary HP, and is not damage for resource triggers. It cannot reduce the donor below 1 unless a card expressly grants a death-triggered effect.

No damage/healing copy repeats the source's costs, procs, resource generation, critical bonus dice, buffs, actions, cooldown resets or duration. Compute fractions once, capped at 100% of one stored source unless an explicit card states a separately priced higher amount. Copies still cause ordinary damage consequences, concentration checks and death. A copy cannot copy another copy. A target/source record must refer to an actual resolved event, not merely a known ability name.

Where a class card calls for a **standard companion** without a more specific profile, use: Small or Medium; AC 12+floor(PB/2); HP 2 L; walking Speed 30 ft; saves equal owner's PB; one melee or ranged attack (reach 5 ft/range 30 ft) at owner's class attack bonus, damage S d6 of the printed type. It has no independent class features, resources, loot, death triggers or extra turns. All companions belonging to one character share one Bonus Action command and **one damaging attack/action total per round** unless a specifically priced feature grants more. Without a command they move and Dodge. Act immediately after owner. A standard companion lasts 1 minute, disappears at 0 HP and cannot be healed for free by dismissing/resummoning. The creation cost must be paid again. Creature-specific stat blocks override this profile only where explicitly printed.

## Ordinary spells: one explicit test configuration

Use the manifest-owned **Core Systems Known Descent V 2** class RP tables and rank costs: rank 0–9 costs 0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26; Grand 32. Follow `src/data/class-spell-progression.js` for each class's rank gates and the existing spell catalog for class/school access. Having enough RP never bypasses a rank gate. Oracle has Revelation Charges, and Soldier/Warrior have no general RP spellcasting. Multiclass spell access is determined separately per class; do not add complete class pools or use total level to unlock a rank. This suite's printed pool tables are single-class; use the existing multiclass pool formula with the new constituent Core V 2 pools for mixed characters.

Four classes have no direct Core V 2 pool row. For this pilot, Crimson Agent uses the Cleric curve multiplied by 0.5; Dragoon, Monk and Thief use that curve multiplied by 0.35, rounded to nearest integer with halves upward, minimum 1. These fallback factors come from the preserved `src/data/resonance-economy.js`; they are explicitly distinguished from direct book tables. The generic Core V 2 Oracle RP row is rejected for this class suite because Oracle's protected class contract uses Revelation Charges only. Oracle never receives RP or ordinary spell access. Retune here means one recovery at the end of a completed short rest, not an unrestricted action.

For a reproducible pilot, retain the protected **Dissonance** layer with Core V 2 numeric RP costs. This combination is a new integration decision: do not also roll a second historical Burn/fizzle system on top of it. Limit=max(4, 2+PB+max(0, casting modifier)). Before a ranked cast, Dissonance at limit/limit+3/limit+6 adds 1/2/3 RP respectively; at limit+6 ordinary casters cannot cast rank 1+. At limit+3 ordinary Overcast is unavailable. A cast then adds base Dissonance 0 at rank 0, 1 at ranks 1–5, 2 at ranks 6–9. Immediate repeated casts of the same named spell add 1, 2, then 3 maximum. Another named spell resets the repeat counter but not accumulated strain. Apply the class's exact cadence reduction/vent; never infer a free RP reduction. Printed class techniques pay printed costs and cause no automatic spell Dissonance unless tagged or expressly described as spells, Echo releases or Matrix casts. For a Mage/Wizard class card tagged as a spell, use the rank printed in normalized data; its rank is fixed at acquisition and does not rise with S. Other techniques are not counterspell able unless their card says so.

Retune recovers max(0, round(max RP/4)+casting modifier), never above maximum, and clears Dissonance. A long rest restores RP and clears Dissonance. Optional 10-minute meditation once/day recovers positive casting modifier RP and reduces Dissonance by PB+positive modifier. A regular turn with no spell or magical class ability loses 1 Dissonance; an Action spent Grounding without casting loses PB instead (not both). Merely ending an encounter does not clear accumulated Dissonance. Refrain survives idle/weapon turns unless a class explicitly clears it. Lich/Necromancer may force ranked casts through Fracture; after resolution take direct unpreventable trauma equal to rank×1/2/3 at the three strained states, minimum 1, based on state before casting. This trauma cannot generate resources or trigger damage-sharing. They still pay RP and meet rank gates.

Generic Overcast is excluded from the initial suite configuration until its options are separately fixed; cards such as Overchannel have their own exact costs and gates. Core V 2's original Burn procedures, older rank×2 costs and smaller companion RP tables remain preserved as alternatives, not silently combined. This configuration is suit able for comparing class drafts, not a claim that all historical magic sources already agree.

## Spell repertoires and acquisition

Preserve explicit class spellbook/preparation rules where given. For classes missing a known-spell count, this suite proposes: full casters know 3 cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10 and choose 2 ranked spells at first spell access plus 1 each later class level; hybrid/half/minor casters know 2 cantrips at first cantrip access and 3 at class 10, and choose 2 ranked spells at first ranked access plus 1 on each later even class level. At a long rest, a known caster may replace one known spell with a legal same-or-lower rank selection. This fills an actual missing rule and does not replace a more specific Druid prepared list or Wizard spellbook. Bonus spells expressly granted by a class are additional. No unnamed or mechanically unfinished catalog spell becomes complete merely by entering this repertoire; select operational spells for the test and record them.

Scheduled selection applies only where the class document says so. At each milestone choose distinct eligible entries; no banked Skill Points. Automatic engines, ASIs, feats, forms and finales do not also consume a choice unless stated. Ordinary-class schedule:4 Base at 1 (at least 2 active), 2 Base at 2; 2 Arch at 3 (at least 1 active); alternating 1 Base/Arch at 4/6/8/11/13/15/17/19 and 1 Arch at 5/7/9; choose Hero at 10 and 2 Hero (at least 1 active), then 1 Hero at 12/14/16/18; finale 20. If a class has no source Arch capstone, level 9 has the printed class-specific grant or another choice, explicitly shown. The individual schedule and prerequisite checks win over this summary. ASI or eligible feat at 4/8/12/16/19, separate from choices, except Oracle uses its explicit 4/8/14/19 schedule. Druid, Oracle and Paladin use their own schedules.

## Shared interpretation

**family.bleeding.** Explicit hostile Bleed classification for immunity, curing and stated eligibility. Class/owner/source timing and caps remain separate. No inherited damage package.

**family.ongoing-fire.** Only explicitly registered creature-attached Burn-style periodic fire. Excludes direct fire, areas, hazards, environmental flames, object ignition, Resonance Burn and names alone.

**periodic.arbitration.** Generic Core and custom groups enter ONE family arbitration at an identical target marker. Within each family at one identical target timing marker, select one stack group by highest expected unmitigated damage then earliest application. Apply source instance caps before comparing. All due groups consume their tick, including non-damaging losers. Different markers and families resolve separately. Stable unique application sequence breaks simultaneous applications in resolution order; lexical group ID is a final implementation tie-break only.

**ownership.** Ordinary your means ownerCharacterId. Explicit class phrases restrict sourceClass. Crimson technical Bleed engine hooks require owned Crimson instances. Suppressed, immune, inactive or expired effects do not satisfy active-effect hooks.

**hp-cure-separation.** HP prohibition prevents regained HP. Legal positive-potential magical healing can still invoke a registered Bleed cure, including Blood Curse CON save; a remover explicitly requiring actual HP gained retains that prerequisite.

**exclusive-periodic-binding.** A textual effect component with a reviewed source-qualified profile creates only that record. Core Bleeding/Burning are fallback identities only for explicit Core applications lacking a more-specific profile. A family tag or display word never also creates a generic record. Two records require two effects explicitly imposed by the operative source.

**immunity-and-periodic-arbitration.** Condition/family immunity prevents initial application. Gained condition/family immunity suppresses an existing record: clocks and due ticks continue, but suppressed records are excluded from damage arbitration and active-effect hooks. Damage-type immunity/resistance does not suppress the record or exclude it from arbitration; choose using unmitigated expectation, then apply defenses.

**recipe-occupancy.** A poison recipe occupies an ongoing-instance slot only while at least one ongoing component remains. Suppression does not erase an existing component; curing/expiry can end it. Resolved one-time critical healing does not occupy a slot. Ending Bloodleech's sole remaining Bleed ends its occupancy without purging other poison or curse records.

**cure-presence-suppression.** SUPERSESSION: Cure/removal tests existing unexpired presence, not current effect activity. Medicine selects one present eligible Bleed; positive-potential legal magical healing invokes each present eligible endpoint (Blood Curse retains CON save); Action/full immersion ends all present ordinary-extinguishable fires. Suppression/acquired condition immunity does not bar these cures or existing permitted ending saves. Damage arbitration and active-effect hooks still exclude suppressed/immune records. Initial immunity prevents new application; ended records cannot resume.

**Application records.** Preserve application ID, owner character, source class/engine, target, DC, damage type, start, remaining ticks or expiry, source stack group, and cure exceptions. “Immune” in an active-effect eligibility check means immunity to the condition/application, not merely immunity to its damage type. Damage immunity does not by itself erase an effect.

**Timing.** Explicit start/end timing wins. An omitted next-turn periodic marker is provisionally end of the next regular target turn. Extra turns add no periodic ticks or ending saves. Outside initiative preserve the clock and consume one due step per complete six seconds; initiative transitions do not duplicate events.

**Bleed treatment.** A WIS (Medicine) Action by self or an adjacent helper selects one ordinary Bleed record before rolling: printed cure DC, otherwise recorded applying effect/class/spell DC, otherwise 10. Success ends that record. One legal magical-healing event with positive pre-cap/pre-prohibition potential ends every eligible automatic-healing-cure record; each Blood Curse instead receives its own CON save. An explicit remover keeps its stated one/all/owner scope.

**Cure presence.** Treatment, magical-healing cure and permitted per-record ending saves can remove a still-present suppressed or condition-immune Bleed/fire record. Cure scope and special prerequisites remain unchanged. Effect eligibility and damage arbitration still exclude suppressed records. Successful removal ends the record permanently; immunity ending cannot restore it.

**Kit exceptions.** A Crimson kit Action consumes one use and ends that source owner's Crimson Bleeds on the victim. A Dragoon kit Action consumes one use and ends the selected Dragoon Bleed. Other records do not silently acquire these kit endpoints.

**Attached fire treatment.** One self/helper extinguish Action or full immersion ends all ordinary-extinguishable attached fires on that creature. Explicit protected-fire exceptions survive. At the end of each regular target turn, after due ticks are consumed, each still-active fire record with future ticks remaining receives its own ending DEX save at its source DC or 10. An indefinite generic fire has future ticks. No ending save is needed after a record's final tick expires.

**Duration changes.** Printed base duration is distinct from an express hard cap. A qualifying refresh never shortens remaining duration. Persistent Bleed normally supplies two turns; Prolonged Suffering changes application/refresh to four only for owned profiles whose printed base is exactly two. Use the greatest legal replacement, not a sum; obey actual hard caps. No source trigger means no refresh, and expired records cannot be refreshed.

# Condition recovery and exposure — provisional procedures

**Reviewed provisional integration, 8 October 2026.** These are fictional game procedures. The sources provide the condition identities, existing dose/tolerance rules, six Exhaustion levels and Intoxication thresholds; the exact generic recovery projects and missing endpoints below are newly authored proposals discussed with GPT. Preserve the original sources. Use with [all 28 conditions](CONDITIONS_PLAYTEST.md) and [HP, Wounds and death](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md).

## Time, costs and checks

A project day is a consecutive 24-hour interval starting when that project begins, not a calendar-date change. A three-day project finishes no earlier than 72 elapsed hours; seven days means at least 168 hours. Only one project of the same kind for the same patient and named condition may be active. Concurrent clocks measure the same elapsed time once; the same active hour or consumed Supply cannot pay two activities. An active practitioner cannot simultaneously perform a long rest. A patient can receive care while resting where the care permits it.

Consume each stated Supply or kit use at the beginning of its attempt or daily work. Interruption does not refund it. Missing a required project day, taking a forbidden dose or receiving forbidden new Exposure ends that attempt; completed costs remain spent, and starting again requires a fresh full project. Merely suppressing symptoms does not interrupt abstinence or time already properly completed.

Project skill checks use the reviewed four-degree task rules. Success and Critical Success give the stated success; Failure and Critical Failure give the stated failure unless specifically differentiated. No extra reward or complication is inferred from an undefined degree. Saving throws remain binary. Use WIS (Medicine), INT (Religion), INT (Arcana), or an INT check using proficiency with alchemist's supplies for Alchemy. These ability/tool assignments are explicit integration choices; an actual feature can supply its printed alternative.

## Exhaustion

The six V6 effects are cumulative: level 1 disadvantage on ability checks; 2 Speed halved; 3 disadvantage on attack rolls and saves; 4 maximum HP halved; 5 Speed zero; 6 death. Compute level-4 maximum as `max(1, floor(otherwise-applicable maximum HP / 2))`. Recompute from the otherwise-applicable maximum whenever it changes. Clamp current HP when the maximum falls; restoring the maximum does not heal. Flat Speed changes apply before halving; a zero-Speed condition overrides the calculation. A maximum-HP reduction alone is not damage and does not trigger a Wound save.

**NEW generic recovery:** At the end of a beneficial eight-hour long rest, remove one Exhaustion level from a living creature at levels 1–5 if it met the campaign's food/water requirements, the originating cause no longer actively imposes or refreshes Exhaustion, and no source-specific rule blocks removal of the chosen level. At most one generic level can be removed per 24 elapsed hours. Specific reviewed effects can remove additional levels as printed. A prerequisite such as Moisture Dependency's one-hour immersion unlocks recovery; it does not itself remove a level unless explicitly stated. Track blocked-source levels separately so another source's removable level may still be selected; the patient chooses a legal level to remove.

Exhaustion 6 causes death. Removing levels from the corpse never revives it. A resurrection effect must also leave the creature below 6 or it immediately dies again. Global Exhaustion, expedition Strain, Warrior serum Strain and Oracle's one-turn Revelation backlash remain separate records; this procedure clears none of those other tracks. See the [Strain namespace candidate](STRAIN_PLAYTEST.md) for its separately recorded review status.

## Dependence and Withdrawal

Preserve Core's existing substance procedures: resolve benefit and crash; a repeat dose before the next long rest requires the substance's dependence CON save; three uses within seven days cause tolerance that halves duration unless doubled; more than two doses before a long rest triggers the substance's severe complication and dependence advancement. This document supplies endpoints, not a replacement substance catalog. Use each item's reviewed dependence DC and severe complication. An item lacking its actual consequence remains in the item review queue rather than gaining an invented generic overdose result.

**Maintenance:** At each completed long rest, a new maintenance dose is due for each named dependence. Withdrawal applies immediately until a qualifying dose is taken after that rest; a dose taken before its completion cannot satisfy the new interval. The dose ends that substance's current symptoms until the next maintenance interval but does not remove dependence. Ordinary consumption time, stock, crash, tolerance and repeated-dose rules still apply. No free dose or Action is granted.

**Tolerance:** Record doses in a rolling seven-day window. After the third completed dose/use within that window, tolerance becomes active; subsequent uses have half duration unless doubled. The third ordinary use is not retroactively shortened. Count a doubled dose as two doses for tolerance, repeated-dose and overdose accounting; resolve its two-dose thresholds as one consumption event, with at most one dependence save for that event. Seven full days with no dose clears tolerance. One long rest does not clear tolerance. Track each substance separately.

**NEW dependence recovery project:** Complete seven consecutive project days without a dose of the named substance. Each day the patient spends one hour in treatment/recovery work and consumes one Supply. Choose Medicine, Religion or Alchemy at project start. At the end of the seventh full day, the designated practitioner (who may be the patient) makes that check against the substance's dependence DC, or NEW DC 14 if a direct Addicted effect supplied no substance DC. Success removes that named Addicted and its associated Withdrawal. Failure removes neither; a new attempt needs a new seven-day project. There is no extra automatic Wound on Critical Failure.

The existing Haven activity “Treat Dependence or Withdrawal” gives advantage on the next recovery check and prevents one ordinary withdrawal escalation after one full day under qualified care. ## Recompute capacity from separate records

Keep base maximum, bonuses, reductions and systemic multipliers separate. Base maximum excludes all modifiers represented separately in this ledger. Never feed a previously modified maximum back into the formula.

First calculate the otherwise-applicable maximum:

    preSystemicMaximum = max(1, baseMaximum + compatibleBonuses − strongestMonkTrauma)

Then apply the reviewed systemic factors against that same value:

    effectiveMaximum = max(1, floor(preSystemicMaximum × systemicFactors))

Expedition Strain4+ contributes3/4 and Exhaustion4+ contributes1/2. Multiply compatible rational factors before rounding once. Base101, Flesh Warden+20, Monk trauma−9 and both factors produce42. Suppressing that trauma produces45; do not subtract the trauma again afterward.

The numerical modifier calculation does not perform lethal-track transitions. Use the separate reviewed life-state procedure when a track actually changes. Merely recomputing maximum HP must not re-kill a living collapsed survivor at track6.

Each application retains its own ID, source, owner, target, magnitude, start/end markers, presence and suppression state, arbitration group and any acquisition/creation snapshot needed for its formula. Keep records even when another stronger application wins. Suppression does not stop clocks.

After any maximum change, clamp current normal HP down only if it exceeds the new maximum. Adding/restoring maximum HP gives no current HP. For cumulative eligible covered loss L: `TotalEntitlement = max(0, min(I, r × min(L, I) − D))` `AdditionalPayment = max(0, TotalEntitlement − prior actual payouts)` Apply the genuine policy terms and remaining insured value. This new partial-loss calculation matches the source whole-loss formula when L = I. A later claim does not restart the deductible or pay the full total again. The same already compensated interest cannot collect twice. Recovery of insured property requires its real return/subrogation adjustment. Give an actual safe-access claim notice within 72 elapsed hours of return; an earlier authenticated notice counts. Declared inability to communicate postpones the deadline until communication is restored, without backdating coverage. Routine examination needs two active hours of qualified work plus real evidence-gathering time. It is not guaranteed payment in two hours. Fraud, undeclared cargo, voluntary abandonment without a prior insured-sacrifice clause, and loss after knowingly ignoring an applicable abort condition are excluded. Insurance supplies money under terms, never new material, HP, souls or a restored person. ### FL-23 — Standing and earned history The new ordinary policy, **standing-v1**, uses an integer from −3 to +3 for each resolved individual/institution relationship: | Score | Description | Ordinary access guide | |---:|---|---| | −3 or −2 | Hated | An actual willing provider, safe intermediary or specific exception; no automatic attack | | −1 | Disliked | The provider's ordinary public dealings under its real restrictions | | 0 | Neutral | Eligibility to ask for public goods, lodging and contracts | | +1 | Liked | Consideration for an offered introduction/license/buyer process | | +2 or +3 | Honored | Consideration for offered bonded storage, credit, sensitive desks or senior audiences | These are opportunities to seek actual services, not granted offices, ownership, credit balances, licenses, waivers or auction admission. Named existing entitlements keep their own terms. Hated with one institution does not ban unrelated public services. Keep +2 and +3 distinct even though both display Honored; absence, unresolved information and hidden data are not an explicit known Neutral 0. Saved standing supplies **no automatic d20 modifier or magic discount**. It changes no RP, RC, spell rank, Dissonance, charges or alignment by itself. Reputation as a CHA skill is a separate applicable check: add proficiency once, not proficiency plus the relationship score. The actual known-buyer mundane sale fraction remains its specific equipment rule. A significant public attributable ordinary event can propose ±1; a major public success/betrayal ±2. Within one subject/institution/scene, add the signed proposals, cap their sum at −2…+2, then apply it to that scene's opening score and clamp the result to −3…+3. Record every event, its contribution, actual applied change and overflow. Recompute from the opening score when opposite events occur; do not exploit the order of saturation. No banked overflow or extra award per witness/report. A campaign-defining exception requires its real distinct event and expressly predeclared magnitude/cap exception. For a genuinely fresh Cult Escapee, bind the full background to actual institutions: former cult Hated/−2, suspicious religious authority Disliked/−1, anti-cult group Liked/+1. This does not target every cult or religious order. Existing earned history is never overwritten by a fresh-start value. ### FL-24 — Haven work, services, learning and recovery A Haven Turn is **24 elapsed hours**, not a token that buys any result. A deal does not create forged authority, a new skill or a free Scribing recipe. Underways Heat is 0–6 for the actual operation/institution pursuit history. Voluntary passengers use their actual seats/custody facts, not captive ownership.
